newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa pulls back further as buyers dry up.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa pulls back further as buyers dry up.

text.p: Cocoa futures turned sharply lower on Wednesday after a volatile session but turnover was modest.
Traders said funds and locals that have taken on long positions in recent days retreated to the sidelines, leaving the market prone to fluctuations.
But losses were regarded as part of a consolidation process following a surge in benchmark May futures to a seven-month high of 1,048 stg on Tuesday.
The May contract shed 18 stg to 1,015 stg a tonne at the close on Wednesday after an intraday bounce to 1,030.
"We had a down movement this morning, we had an attempted rally and a subsequent fall," said one trader.
"There is no liquidity. 500 Aas and 1,400 crosses."
The crosses included 200-lots of June/June dealt at 50 stg in a total turnover of 4,090 lots.

Reaction was muted to a fall Ghana's weekly cocoa purchase figures which are now tailing off. Purchases were 2,428 tonnes in the 20th week ending February 27, down from 5,702 the week before. The cumulative amounted to 294,216 lots.
"It's the end of the season. There wasn't much impetus there," said the trader.
New York cocoa prices also pressed lower in morning dealings after a round of local selling, believed to be speculative profit-taking.

Traders there reckoned sentiment was partly dampened after an upward reassessment of the Ivorian harvest by broker GNI on Tuesday. It saw the crop reaching 1.1 million tonnes based on the strong set of arrivals data.
But some were concerned that funds, which have already covered shorts and shifted to longs, may be reluctant to buy more.
Technical support is pegged at the chart gap extending from 989 to 982 basis LIFFE May. If 982 breaks, analysts will be looking for a sell-off.
